'''''The History and Development of the Human Languages, Volume I''''' was a document written by [[Doctor/Legends|Dr.]] [[Arner Figgis]]. The article was about the history of [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]], focusing particularly on its roots in [[Old Coruscanti]]. It was referenced as being "amazing" and an "invaluable resource" in the ''Further readings'' section of ''[[The Written Word: A Brief Introduction to the Writing Systems of Galactic Basic]]'', written by Dr. [[Milanda Vorgan]].<ref name="The Written Word" />

==Behind the scenes==
''The History and Development of the Human Languages, Volume I'' was first referenced in the [[StarWars.com]] [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]] article, ''[[The Written Word]]'' in [[2010]], under the "Further readings" section.<ref name="The Written Word" /> Author [[John Hazlett]] wrote in his blog that the section was to give his article some in-universe context.<ref name="Blog">{{Blog|JSarek|8|Endnotes for The Written Word}}</ref>

Hazlett attributed the fictional work to the character of Arner Figgis, who originated from the [[August]] [[1995]] [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 7|''Star Wars Adventure Journal'' 7]]. According to Hazlett, the character's personality in another in-universe work, ''[[Old Corellian: A Guide for the Curious Scholar]]'', leant itself to the verbose titles of older "[[Wikipedia:British|British]] [[Wikipedia:Masterpiece|magna opera]]," such as [[Wikipedia:Edward Gibbon|Edward Gibbon's]] [[Wikipedia:The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire|''The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire'']] and [[Wikipedia:Winston Churchill|Winston Churchill's]] [[Wikipedia:A History of the English-Speaking Peoples|''A History of the English-Speaking Peoples'']].<ref name="Blog" />
